title: Learning curves and the service's catalog: what a kind of model takes, said only from three builds
request: What it takes to build each kind of model: how many labels, how often it meets its bar, its cost and time.
plan: Curves from the tutor's kept model cards.
The catalog per problem kind, aggregates only.
Fewer than three builds: say so.

decisions.why: A median of one or two builds would be one business's figures.

findings.defect: The catalog and the playbook could show one workspace's figures alone.
findings.scenario: Three builds all from one business gave that business's own met share and median cost.
findings.cause: Only the build count was gated.
findings.fix: A figure needs three builds in three workspaces.

findings.defect: The catalog could not say how many labels a kind needs.
findings.scenario: labels_needed said labelled rows were not counted apart.
findings.cause: Only the table's rows were read.
findings.fix: A build's labelled rows: its final record's training and holdout rows, in bands; the kind's curve by that band and the bands of the builds that met their bar.

outcome: The catalog says a figure only where it rests on enough builds.
lessons: Write fixtures from the code that writes the records (a stage record copied from the engine), never from memory: invented shapes made every test pass while every real build was judged wrong.
risks: Three builds from one workspace still describe that one workspace.
